name: DVB-S IP (satellite)
label: DVB-S IP
notes: IP carried over DVB-S and DVB-S2 satellite links, decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. It is a status row, as DVB-T's: one job locks to the carrier nearest the centre of its band (an intermediate frequency from a dish's LNB, which is the operator's) and reports its state; the IP datagrams it carries are the packets. An event comes at first lock (or after 2 s), then when a member changes and at least every 2 s: `locked` (the error correction delivers), and while locked `standard` (`dvbs`, `dvbs2`, or `dvbs2x` when OnAir sees S2X signalling), `symbol_rate` (symbols a second, to 1 ksym/s), `modcod` (as OnAir spells it, for example `QPSK 2/3`, with short or medium frames, pilots and VCM added), `snr_db` (Es/N0 from the symbols) and `datagrams` (the IP datagrams so far; `snr_db` and `datagrams` make no event of their own). The job's band is passed to the wrapper as `--width`: what lies outside it is filtered off before the receiver, because OnAir cannot bound its symbol rate search, so the carrier it can take has a symbol rate of at most the band's width; give a band that holds the whole carrier (a wider carrier is narrowed and does not lock). The handler takes 10 MHz of IQ; 4 MHz is enough for MPE and ULE, and DVB-S2X beyond OnAir's own is not decoded. GSE is read from the DVB-S2 frames; MPE and ULE from the transport stream. Each whole IP datagram goes to a packet capture as it is (link type 101); a transport stream with no IP is decoded and dropped (no service list), encrypted payloads are given as received and nothing is decrypted. OnAir prints one line on stderr that its GPU decoder is switched off (the wrapper runs the decoders on the CPU): expected. Ranges and bands: none; DVB-S and DVB-S2 (ETSI EN 300 421 and EN 302 307) are carried on a dish's intermediate frequency, which the operator's LNB and radio decide, so no radio-frequency range is given and identify tries the row as asked, on the band it was asked for, wherever that is. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 1.02 of a core and the node 0.25 of a core (load average 4.3 to 4.1). Measured with the band 10 MHz wide on OnAir's 5 Msym/s DVB-S2 test carrier carrying GSE.
